questions.question: DNA is described as a long chemical molecule made of two chains of smaller units. If a scientist breaks all the chemical bonds holding the two chains together but leaves the bonds within each chain intact, what would they observe?
options: The DNA would break down into individual small chemical units.
The DNA would separate into two distinct, intact single chains.
The DNA would remain a double helix but lose its chemical code.
The DNA would immediately form a single, longer continuous chain.

questions.question: A student extracts all of the genetic material from a single muscle cell of a mouse. Which of the following terms correctly describes the entire collection of DNA that has been extracted?
options: A gene
The genome
A chromosome
A double helix

questions.question: If you look at the structure of DNA as a ladder, what represents the "rungs" (links across the middle) and what represents the "sides" of the ladder?
options: The sides are the single chemical units; the rungs are the double helix spiral bonds.
The sides are the nuclear membranes; the rungs are the tightly packed chromosome fibres.
The sides are the two spiralled chemical chains; the rungs are the chemical links connecting them.
The sides are the genes; the rungs are the non-coding sections of DNA.

questions.question: A physical model of DNA made of plastic pieces is useful for showing how the two chains connect, but what is a limitation or weakness of using such a physical model?
options: It cannot show that DNA is composed of two chains spiralled in a double helix.
It cannot show the dynamic, chemical processes and reactions that occur when DNA is used by the cell.
It cannot represent the fact that DNA is stored inside the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
It fails to show that genes contain instructions for inherited features.

questions.question: When extracting DNA from a kiwi fruit, why can we see the extracted DNA in our test tube with the naked eye, even though individual DNA molecules are far too small to be seen?
options: The DNA molecules expand and grow larger when they come into contact with cold alcohol.
The extraction process causes millions of microscopic DNA molecules to clump together.
The DNA molecules absorb the green pigment of the kiwi fruit, making them visible.
The filter paper aligns the individual strands so they reflect light together.

questions.question: How are the genome, DNA, and chromosomes physically organized within a eukaryotic cell?
options: The genome is a single gene that is divided into chromosomes made of small DNA molecules.
Chromosomes are made of tightly wound DNA molecules, which together make up the genome.
DNA is made of chromosomes that are packed together to form a genome.
Chromosomes are small units of the genome that are connected by DNA chains.

questions.question: If we compare the genetic material in a human skin cell to that in a bacterium, which of the following describes a key structural difference in how they are stored?
options: Human cells store 23 pairs of chromosomes in the nucleus, whereas bacteria store a single chromosome in the cytoplasm.
Human cells store 23 single chromosomes in the nucleus, whereas bacteria store 23 pairs in the cytoplasm.
Human cells store one chromosome in the nucleus, whereas bacteria store 23 pairs in the cytoplasm.
Human cells store chromosomes in the cytoplasm, whereas bacteria store them in the nucleus.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between a chromosome, a gene, and their functions?
options: A gene is a packed chromosome that controls the cell membrane's structure.
A chromosome is a small section of a gene that contains instructions for one specific feature.
A gene is a specific section of DNA on a chromosome that stores instructions for a particular feature or process.
A chromosome is the chemical unit that links the two chains of a gene together.

questions.question: If a scientist removes a section of "non-coding DNA" from an organism's genome, what is the most likely direct consequence?
options: The organism will completely lose the ability to inherit any traits from its parents.
The cell may lose the ability to control when or how specific genes are turned on and used.
The cell will immediately stop producing all chemical units that form the DNA chains.
The chromosomes will instantly unwind and spill out of the nucleus.

questions.question: A student is looking under a microscope at an unknown cell. They observe that the cell has a cytoplasm and a cell membrane, but no nucleus. Where would they find the genetic material of this organism?
options: Free-floating inside the cytoplasm, because it is a bacterium.
Bound inside a vacuole, because it is an animal cell.
Within the cell membrane, because it is a fungus.
No genetic material exists because cells without a nucleus do not have DNA.

questions.question: How does DNA act as an "instruction manual" for an organism's life processes and features?
options: The physical weight of the DNA molecules determines which features develop.
The specific sequence of smaller molecules along the DNA chains forms a code that the cell decodes to build features.
DNA molecules physically move to different parts of the body to form physical tissues like muscle and bone.
The double helix shape acts as a physical template that directly shapes the cells of the organism.

questions.question: Why do brothers and sisters from the same biological parents look similar to each other and to their parents, but are not identical?
options: They inherit genetic material from only one parent, but which parent they inherit it from is completely random.
They inherit different mixtures of genetic material from both parents, leading to shared but unique combinations of features.
They inherit all their features from their father, and their environment makes them look like their mother.
They inherit genetic material from both parents, but the material is identical for every child.

questions.question: Except in the case of identical twins, offspring of the same parents show variation. What is the biological reason for this variation among offspring?
options: Offspring receive different combinations of genes from their parents, creating unique genetic instructions.
Offspring change their genetic material after birth based on their environment.
Only one parent passes on genetic material, and it changes depending on the age of the parent.
The non-coding DNA completely overrides the genes during growth.

questions.question: During fertilisation, an egg cell and a sperm cell fuse. How does this process relate to heredity?
options: It allows environmental changes from the parents' lives to be copied into the offspring's cells.
It combines genetic material from both parents, passing on the instructions that determine the offspring's biological features.
It destroys the parents' original DNA so that the offspring can develop entirely new, random traits.
It converts non-coding DNA into active genes to ensure the offspring is a new species.

questions.question: A professional athlete trains hard and develops extremely strong muscles. If they have a child, why won't the child automatically be born with extremely strong muscles?
options: Muscle strength is not controlled by any genetic material.
Only features programmed by instructions in the genetic material can be inherited, not traits acquired through training.
Acquired traits are only passed on from the mother, not the father.
The child will inherit the strength, but only after they reach adulthood.

questions.question: Which of the following features is caused entirely by environmental factors and cannot be passed on to offspring?
options: A scar on a person's arm from a childhood accident
The natural colour of a person's eyes
The shape of a person's earlobes
Having a hereditary blood group

questions.question: A group of scientists is studying a plant. They find some plants have red flowers and some have green leaves with spots caused by a leaf-mining insect. How should these two features be classified?
options: Red flowers are genetic; insect spots are genetic.
Red flowers are environmental; insect spots are genetic.
Red flowers are genetic; insect spots are environmental.
Red flowers are environmental; insect spots are environmental.

questions.question: Why did it take from the discovery of DNA in 1869 until 1953 for scientists to work out its double helix structure?
options: Scientists had to wait until the 1950s for the technology to extract DNA from cells to be invented.
It required scientists to share different pieces of evidence, collaborate, and build physical models to interpret the clues.
No one believed DNA was important until 1953, so no research was conducted on it.
The structure of DNA actually changed over time due to evolution.

questions.question: What crucial evidence did Rosalind Franklin's team in London contribute to the discovery of the structure of DNA in 1952?
options: They built the first three-dimensional cardboard model of the double helix.
They proved that bacteria do not have a nucleus.
They used X-rays to capture an image that indicated the helical shape of DNA.
They extracted DNA from fruit for the very first time.

questions.question: How did James Watson and Francis Crick use the scientific work of others to complete their model of DNA?
options: They used the X-ray picture taken by Franklin's team to work out and build a physical model of the double helix structure.
They proved that Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images were completely incorrect and built a different model.
They used the image to show that DNA is a single straight chain without any links.
They used it to discover that DNA is stored in the cytoplasm of human cells.
